Interesting - we got past `hid.Device` AttributeError.

Now the failure is `hid.device.read` with `ValueError: not open`. The device object was constructed via `hid`.

Cython-hidapi's `hid.device(path=...)` does not open the device automatically. It requires an explicit `open()` or `open_path()` call. The ctypes `hid.Device(path=...)` constructor opens the device immediately. This API difference explains the `not open` error.

The fix requires instantiating `hid.device()` and then calling `open_path()` separately. I will inspect the cython-hidapi API in the virtual environment to confirm the exact method.

Fixed and rebuilt.

`hidapi` (Cython) doesn’t have `hid.Device`, and `hid.device(path=...)` doesn’t open the handle — it needs `open_path`. Open path in `emotiv_base.py` now handles both APIs; `main.spec` comment updated. Fresh `dist/emotiv_lsl.exe` ran past HID open with no `AttributeError` (stayed up until stopped).
